title: Panzanella
subtitle: Tuscan bread and tomato salad
excerpt: Tuscany's genius bread salad: stale bread soaked in water, squeezed out, and tossed with the ripest summer tomatoes, red onion, basil, and a generous amount of olive oil and red wine vinegar. At its best in peak tomato season.

recipe.sourceNotes: Panzanella is a Tuscan peasant salad that makes use of stale bread by soaking it in water to rehydrate it, then squeezing out the excess moisture and mixing it with ripe tomatoes, onion, basil, and a dressing of olive oil and vinegar. The dish is a study in simplicity: the bread absorbs the tomato juices and dressing and becomes pleasantly soft and savoury rather than merely soggy. The key to panzanella is ripe, flavourful tomatoes; out-of-season tomatoes produce a pale, watery version that misses the point entirely. The dish is best made 30 minutes before serving to allow the bread to absorb the dressing, and then eaten at room temperature rather than chilled.

content.text: Use bread that is at least a day old; fresh bread becomes an unpleasant mush. Soak it briefly in water to soften, then squeeze very firmly until almost dry. The tomatoes should be at peak ripeness; the juice they release is a key part of the dressing. Rest the finished salad for 30 minutes before serving to let the bread absorb the flavours.

items.preparation: very ripe; a mixture of varieties; roughly chopped
very thinly sliced; soaked in cold water for 10 minutes to mellow

content.text: Soak the torn bread in cold water for 5 minutes. Squeeze out as much water as possible until the bread is moist but not dripping. Break it into rough pieces in a large bowl.
Add the tomatoes (and any juice that runs out), drained red onion, and cucumber. Pour over the olive oil and vinegar. Season generously. Toss to combine.
Leave to rest for 30 minutes at room temperature. Taste and adjust the seasoning and vinegar. Scatter with torn basil and serve at room temperature.
